title: Variadic and anonymous functions, and closures

videos.script: Lesson 20 said a call passes exactly as many arguments as a function has parameters. Yet Println has taken any number of arguments since lesson 4. {{variadic}} This lesson starts with how. Three dots before a type, and a function takes any number of arguments. Pass a slice with three dots after it, and the function gets your slice itself, so it can change your elements. {{values}} Then functions as values. A function can sit in a variable, go into another function, and come back out of one. It does not even need a name. The standard library's sort takes one, to learn what order you want. {{closures}} Last, closures. A function made inside another one keeps the variables around it alive. Two of them can share one variable. {{loop}} And that explains a change in Go 1.22, where every turn of a loop got a variable of its own. By the end you can read a function that returns a function, and say what it remembers.
